**The notes below went into the DEC-1102 brief. Keep them for its review brief.**

**Notes for the pull request 2 brief** (from the proposal and the ruling):
1. One module (`web/src/data/scryfallLimiter.ts`) sends every request to `api.scryfall.com`. Bucket 1 holds `/cards/named` and `/cards/collection`: a request starts 600 ms or more after the last start and after the last answer. Bucket 2 holds `/cards/autocomplete`: 120 ms.
2. The 429 rule: a 429 or a rejected `fetch` to that host stops both buckets for 30 s; then one request; the stop doubles up to 5 minutes. The stop time lives in `localStorage`; `navigator.locks` makes two tabs share bucket 1.
3. `cardCache.seed()` makes loaded entries from `card-metadata.json` (`image`, `usd`; the keys of DEC-1075). `CardTile.tsx` sends no request to `/data/images/cards/`. The hover layer and the commander art take the address on `cards.scryfall.io` from the entry. No `format=image` address remains.
4. `cardCache.fetch()` is public and skips the queue (`cardCache.ts`); remove it or send it through the limiter.
5. A stored image address that fails falls back to one lookup through the limiter, at most once a card in 24 h (Scryfall can retire a card id).
6. `loader.ts:388` writes `card-metadata.json` to `localStorage` (1 h lifetime, `:243`). Ask for the total characters in storage before and after, and for the `gv1-card:` entries of seeded names to go.
7. R2: the stop line on /shopping says that the refresh is paused, the date of the prices shown and the clock time of the next try; `role="status"`; it does not say that Scryfall asked.
8. `Shopping.tsx:799` (the footer text) gets the file's price date.
9. The stub: image addresses from the file; the option `cards: 'none'` also removes the prices from `/data/card-metadata.json`; one fixture check fails a test when a 2-a-second method got more than 2 requests in any second; one option answers 429 with no CORS header from request n.
10. Unit cases: for 88 names no window of 1 s holds more than 2 starts (answers after 0 ms and 150 ms); after a 429, 0 requests in 30 s and then 1; after a second 429, 0 in 60 s; a rejected `fetch` gives the same; a new cache instance reads the stop from storage.
11. Web rules for the brief: one `GRIMOIRE_E2E_PORT` value for the tree, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, a new spec imports from `./support/test`, the mutant rules, `document.fonts.ready` before a height.
12. Between pull requests 2 and 3, /combos art takes about 12 s and /shopping shows the file's prices. Say so in the merge record.
13. **The three keys are in PR #24's file** (DEC-1075 hand-back `36c6954c`). `Sol Ring` reads `"image": "front/8/e/8ee443cc-e17a-493b-9c93-1f9e141a30e4.jpg?1789644446", "usd": 1.42, "eur": 1.06`. `https://cards.scryfall.io/<size>/<image>` is Scryfall's own address for `small`, `normal`, `large` and `art_crop`; the pipeline checked `small`, `large` and `art_crop` for all 1,504 cards of the live run.
14. **50 of the 1,556 names have `usd` `null` (41 deck cards), and 51 have `eur` `null`.** The printing that Scryfall returns has no non-foil price (not released, digital only or foil only). The app shows no price for them today either: four `/cards/named` lookups at 22:26Z returned the same printings as the batch. Pull request 2 shows "no price" for `null`, as today. DEC-1079 holds the fix in the pipeline.
15. **Pull request 2 bumps the version of the persisted copy** (`loader.ts:224` records the bump of DEC-940). A browser that holds a copy reads entries without the new keys until then.
16. **The file has 761,602 bytes** (582,504 before PR #24). `writePersisted` (`loader.ts:332-345`) catches the quota error of `localStorage`. Note 6 asks for the totals.
17. **`image` holds the front face only.** The DEC-1080 review (item 5e) found no back-face image in `web/src` (`git grep`), so no page loses one.
18. **`data/card-metadata.meta.json` holds `prices_as_of`** (`2026-10-13T21:56:40+00:00` in PR #24), `count` and `source`. Note 8 reads that date. Every run of the pipeline asks for every name, so one date is true for every price.
19. **`mana_cost` of a two-part card reads `A // B`** in the file for 44 keys: the full names and their front faces (DEC-1080 item 5e). Today's lookup takes the front face's cost first (`web/src/data/cardCache.ts:203`), and `CardTile.tsx:95` shows it. So `seed()` must not copy the file's `mana_cost` for a two-part card.

---

**Leg 1 is a proposal: no code and no pull request.** Measure what the app sends to Scryfall, and propose how it stays inside Scryfall's limits. I rule on the proposal, and the build is leg 2. If the design changes what the owner sees, I ask the owner before leg 2. Proposer: you (Founding Engineer, `4e51e111`). You read `fetchOne` and the four call sites for DEC-1067 today, and your queue is empty. Tier 2, priority high. Budget about 60 minutes.

## Why
- **Scryfall's limits** (`https://scryfall.com/docs/api/rate-limits`, read by me on 2026-10-13): `/cards/named`, `/cards/search`, `/cards/random` and `/cards/collection` allow 2 requests a second each. Every other method allows 10 a second. The image host `*.scryfall.io` has no limit. A 429 limits the caller for 30 seconds. The page says "It is not acceptable to ignore HTTP 429 responses", and an application that keeps overloading the API can be banned.
- **The app sends one `/cards/named` lookup every 120 ms** (`web/src/data/cardCache.ts:40`, `THROTTLE_MS`). The comment at `:13-14` cites an older guideline of 50 ms between calls. /shopping sent 88 lookups in 11.6 s, which is 7.6 a second (DEC-1045 baseline, comment `e6d99397`).
- **A 429 does not stop the app.** `fetchOne` waits for `retry-after`, or 750 ms and then 1,500 ms, and tries the same card up to three times (`cardCache.ts:180-190`). `ERROR_RETRY_MS` at `:41` is 30 s. I have not read what the queue does meanwhile: item 2.
- **Two components send image lookups on the same method, outside the queue:** `web/src/components/global/GV1CardHoverLayer.tsx:19` (`format=image&version=large`, one for each hover) and `web/src/components/molecules/GV1CommanderArt.tsx:16` (`format=image&version=art_crop`).
- `web/src/data/cardAtlas.ts:164` calls `/cards/autocomplete`, which allows 10 a second.
- **The requests leave the user's browser.** The owner uses the app from the address that the deck work's card tools use. A limit or a ban on that address stops both.
- In the baseline run on `main` (two workers), Scryfall rejected 1,158 of 1,280 card lookups (90 %). What one user with one page gets is not measured yet: item 1.
- The e2e stub (PR #19, merged at `a645b74`) never answers 429, so no case shows this fault.

## Facts on `main` at `a645b74`
- The repository already holds most of what a lookup returns. `data/card-metadata.json` has 1,552 cards by name with `mana_cost`, `cmc` and `type_line`. `data/spellbook/price-index.json` has `[eur, usd]` by normalized name, built by `scripts/build_price_index.py` from Scryfall's bulk export. 1,484 of the 1,552 names have a USD price there (your DEC-1067 item 5c). Neither file holds an image address or a Scryfall id.
- The app already loads the price index for the Combo Lab (`web/src/data/prices.ts`).
- A loaded entry lives 24 hours in `localStorage` under `gv1-card:` (`cardCache.ts:38-39`).
- `/cards/collection` takes up to 75 identifiers in one POST.
- The stub is `web/tests/support/scryfall.ts`. It answers the requests that the app sends to a Scryfall host today; a new method needs a new answer there.

## Ask
1. **Measure what one user sends today, under the stub.** For /shopping (default selection), the deck guide with the most cards, /codex, /compare, and one hover over ten card names: the count of requests by method, the peak in one second, and the time to the last answer. Use the stub's log (the `scryfall-stub` attachment) or your counter from DEC-1067. Send no request to the live API for this item.
2. **Say what the app does on a 429 today.** Read the code, then take one reading with a fake `fetch` in a scratch unit file: after the first 429, how many requests does the app send in the next 30 seconds for a page of 88 cards?
3. **Propose at least these three designs.** For each: the requests that one user sends for each page of item 1 (by method, with the peak in one second), what the user sees and when (first paint, prices, art), the files that change, what the stub must answer, the unit and e2e cases that would prove the limit, the engineer hours, and the risks.
   - **A. Batch.** Card facts come through `/cards/collection` (88 cards are 2 requests). Image addresses come from the answer's `image_uris`, so no `format=image` lookup remains. One limiter holds every request to `api.scryfall.com` under the limit of its method. A 429 stops the queue for 30 seconds.
   - **B. Repository data first.** Mana cost, mana value, type line and price come from files that the app already ships. Scryfall answers only what the files lack: the images, and a card outside the data. Say what the pipeline must add (`scripts/`, `data/`) so that a page of deck cards needs no API call at all, and how old a price can then be.
   - **C. The smallest change.** The limiter and the 429 rule alone, at 2 a second. /shopping then needs 44 s for 88 cards; say what the user sees in that time.
   - Add a design of your own if you see a better one.
4. **Recommend one design**, and say what you would not do.

## Rules
- Change no tracked file. Open no branch and no pull request.
- **At most 10 requests to the live API in this leg**, by `curl`, at most one a second, only to read an answer's shape (for example `/cards/collection` with a `//` name and with a front-face name). Quote each command in the proposal.
- **No e2e run on a tree without the stub.** `main` has the stub since `a645b74`.
- If you run Playwright: use a scratch tree `wt-dec<N>` (`<N>` is this issue's number) from `origin/main`, with `git worktree add --detach wt-dec<N> origin/main` and `npm ci` in its `web/`. Set `GRIMOIRE_E2E_PORT=14531` on every run. Before the hand-back, remove the tree: `git status --porcelain` prints nothing, then `git worktree remove <path>` (never `--force`), then `git worktree prune`. Keep scratch files outside the tree.
- Set `HOME="$PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_HOST_HOME"` for `gh` and for every `git` command.
- Set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_HOST_HOME/Library/Caches/ms-playwright"` for every Playwright run. Without it every case fails at launch.
- Do not stop or use another agent's server, and do not touch another agent's tree. Other agents' trees on 2026-10-13: `wt-dec1062`, `wt-dec1063` (PR #20 fix round, live), `wt-dec1064` and the PR #22 review tree `wt-dec1064-review`.
- The harness follow-up of DEC-1067 (B1 and your notes) is next in your queue. It changes `web/tests/support/`. Leg 2 of this issue starts after it.

## Handoff
Post the proposal as one comment on this issue. Put the recommendation first, then the measurements of items 1 and 2, then one section for each design.

Then send one PATCH on this issue as the last action of your run:
- `assigneeAgentId`: the CEO (`f9427c33-d719-4fd5-a3c5-cd2f65dd01e8`).
- `status`: `in_review`.
- `executionPolicy.monitor`: `nextCheckAt` 30 minutes ahead, `scheduledBy: "assignee"`, and `notes` under 500 characters that name the hand-back comment.

The assignment wakes the CEO, who rules on the design and opens leg 2. The monitor wakes the CEO when the server skips that wake; it skipped five hand-backs on 2026-10-13. If the server answers 422 `invalid_issue_disposition`, send the same PATCH again with `nextCheckAt` about ten hours ahead. Never set `done`; only the CEO closes the issue (DEC-970).

The hand-back PATCH ends your run at once. For a question in the middle of the leg, finish the parts that the question does not touch, post the question on this issue (question, evidence, readings, your recommendation) and hand back with the same PATCH. Do not open a child issue assigned to the CEO: the server refuses it (409 `delegation_cycle`).

ancestors.title: Web e2e: answer Scryfall from repository data in Playwright, and take the preview port from an environment variable (DEC-1044 N15, DEC-1026 N16)
ancestors.description:
Make the web e2e suite independent of the live Scryfall API and of port 4173. Test harness only: `web/playwright.config.ts`, `web/tests/`, and the smallest hook in `web/src` if your design needs one.

**Why.**
- Every page the suite loads asks `api.scryfall.com` for each card on it, and no spec on `main` stubs a Scryfall route (`git grep -n "page.route" origin/main -- web/tests` prints one line, the `candidates.json` route at `dec1028-apothecary-followups.spec.ts:19`). During the DEC-1044 review, after several local runs, Scryfall answered 429 to the reference Mac for some minutes (verdict `ba06cc6d`, note N15). While that lasts, no price and no card art arrives in any browser on the Mac. The Scryfall tools that the deck work needs use the same address.
- The specs measure layout with whatever card data has arrived. The Shopping summary's width depends on the price line ("26/781 priced" against "740/781 priced"). That is how PR #11's 977 px figure passed its own checks and failed the review (DEC-1044 D1). The DEC-1026 review saw one screenshot differ between two captures by live prices.
- Playwright reuses whatever listens on port 4173 (`reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`). On the shared Mac a review run measured another tree's server and read 26 failed in 8.8 s; the run was void (DEC-1026 N16). Each reviewer now writes a scratch config on a private port.
- The wait on the live API has now failed a hosted run. On PR #11 at `01edc8e` (run 38413091908, attempt 1), `dec184-visual-qa` hit the 30 s test timeout three times at `dec184-visual-qa.spec.ts:178`, the `networkidle` wait on /shopping: `1 failed, 1 flaky, 5 did not run, 52 passed`. No assertion failed. The CEO re-ran the job once, and attempt 2 read `59 passed`. It is the only failed attempt in the last 25 runs of the workflow.
- Your readings of that wait (DEC-1044 delta verdict `836929ea`, N2), at 375 px in the spec's page order (/codex, the first deck, /compare, /shopping), with local card answers:

| Each card answer takes | /shopping reaches network idle after | Four pages take |
|---|---|---|
| 0 ms, PR #11 merged with `main` | 10.6 s | 13.6 s |
| 0 ms, `main` | 10.6 s | 13.5 s |
| 250 ms, PR #11 merged with `main` | 31.2 s | 35.6 s |
| 250 ms, `main` | 31.2 s | 35.5 s |

  /shopping asks for 82 cards, one at a time and 120 ms apart, on both trees. The test has 30 s, so on the reference Mac it fails once the answers average about 200 ms.
- The 120 ms queue stays under the stub. 82 cards take about 10 s, and 1,169 cards (every deck plus brewing) take about 140 s. In the DEC-1044 measurements you and the Frontend Engineer both paired `page.route` with a seeded `gv1-card:` cache for that reason (hand-back `c0f18df9` on DEC-1017). Say in the hand-back whether your helper can seed the cache for a spec that needs every price in, and what a spec with the default selection waits for.

Tier 1. Implementer: Design System Engineer (`8ea33a50`). You served card answers from repository data by `page.route` in the DEC-1044 review, so the method is yours. Reviewer at hand-back: Frontend Engineer (`bc5c0753`), who owns the specs; the CEO opens the review issue. Reviewer and implementer stay separate.

## Facts on `main` (`090a151`, read again on 2026-10-13 after the PR #11 merge)
- Four call sites: `web/src/data/cardCache.ts:176` (`/cards/named?fuzzy=`, one request for each card name, retried on 429; the price comes from `prices.usd` and the images from `image_uris`), `web/src/data/cardAtlas.ts:164` (`/cards/autocomplete`), `web/src/components/global/GV1CardHoverLayer.tsx:19` and `web/src/components/molecules/GV1CommanderArt.tsx:16` (`/cards/named?…&format=image`, an image redirect).
- Repository data: `data/card-metadata.json` holds 1,552 cards by name (`cmc`, `colors`, `mana_cost`, `oracle_text`, `power`, `toughness`, `type_line`). `data/spellbook/price-index.json` holds 32,141 lower-case names with two numbers each; read its generator before you choose which number is the USD price. Your DEC-1044 run answered 1,552 cards, 1,484 of them with a USD price.
- Ten specs on `main`, and each imports `test` from `@playwright/test`: `combo-lab`, `dec1008-root-overflow`, `dec1019-root-clip`, `dec1021-selector-pill`, `dec1028-apothecary-followups`, `dec181-qa`, `dec184-visual-qa`, `dec185-manifest-sort`, `dec942-owned-quota` and `smoke`. `dec1028-apothecary-followups.spec.ts:19` routes one `candidates.json` request; no other spec routes a request.
- Totals on `main` at `090a151` (push run 38420852874, first attempt): vitest 33 files and 365 tests, Playwright `62 passed (7.0m)`, lint 0 errors and 10 warnings.
- **PR #14 (DEC-1048) merged at `5cfefd9` on 2026-10-13 16:05Z.** `main` now holds an eleventh spec, `tests/dec1048-selector-rail.spec.ts` (11 cases, yours; it imports `test` from `@playwright/test` at `:15`). The reviewer's run on that `web` tree (`93cd2acb…`) read vitest 33 files and 370 tests and Playwright 73 passed. Convert it when you merge `origin/main`.
- One web pull request is open and in review: PR #15 (DEC-1052) edits `tests/dec1028-apothecary-followups.spec.ts`.
- DEC-1063 (Frontend Engineer, started 16:05Z) will add a twelfth spec, `tests/dec1063-selector-unstyled-mount.spec.ts`. Its brief carries the same rule: the pull request that merges second converts.
- `web/qa-screenshots/dec-184/findings.json` is no longer tracked (PR #11), so an e2e run leaves the checkout clean.
- `web/package.json` `preview` is `vite preview --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4173`. `playwright.config.ts` names 4173 twice. CI (`.github/workflows/web-ci.yml`, job `e2e`, `ubuntu-latest`) runs `npm run test:e2e`.

## Ask
1. **Measure first.** Run the full suite once on `main` with a request counter. Quote the number of requests to `api.scryfall.com` by endpoint, and to every other third-party host by name (the font hosts, Scryfall's image host, any other). This is the baseline. It is the only run against the live API that this issue needs.
2. **Answer Scryfall from repository data in every spec.** After the change no e2e request reaches a Scryfall host.
   - The named lookup gives the same answer for the same card on every run (price, mana cost, type line).
   - Images: one fixed local placeholder is enough, because no spec measures the art. Say what you serve.
   - A card name the repository data lacks gets a 404, as Scryfall gives. List those names and the count.
   - The design is yours: a shared `test` fixture that every spec imports, a context-level route, or a base URL set at build time. Give one sentence on why.
3. **The stub is on by default, and a spec cannot skip it by accident.** Add a guard that fails the run and names the request when one reaches a Scryfall host. Say how the guard catches a new spec that imports `@playwright/test` directly.
4. **Keep both card states.** A spec can ask for "no card answers" (every lookup fails), so a layout can be measured with no prices. DEC-1044 measured each layout in both states.
5. **The product does not change.** The production build still calls `https://api.scryfall.com`. If your design touches `web/src`, quote the URL string from the built bundle as proof.
6. **Preview port from an environment variable.** `playwright.config.ts` reads the port from a variable (name it; the default stays 4173, so CI and a bare `npm run test:e2e` work as they do now). When the variable is set, `reuseExistingServer` is `false`, so the run cannot measure another tree's server.
7. **Document both** in `web/README.md` beside the `npm run test:e2e` line (line 16): the stub, the "no card answers" switch and the port variable.
8. **Leave room for the font hosts.** DEC-1043 (yours) adds a fonts-blocked case. Shape the helper so that case can block `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com` with one option. Do not add the case here.
9. **Start `web-ci` on `data/**` too.** Add `'data/**'` to both `paths` lists in `.github/workflows/web-ci.yml` (`push` and `pull_request`). Today the workflow starts only on `web/**` and on its own file. But the suite reads `data/` through the preview server (`web/vite.config.ts:9`), and after item 2 it also reads `data/card-metadata.json` and the price index. So a pull request or a push that changes only `data/` runs no e2e case, and a data change can break a spec with no red check. Example: `dec1028-apothecary-followups.spec.ts` needs the `removal-board` gap in stampede-acres' `metrics.json` (DEC-1031 N8). Do this item last: the trigger is safe only when no case depends on the live Scryfall API.

## If a spec's reading moves
The overflow specs will now always measure with the prices in. If a spec that passes on `main` fails under the stub, do not loosen its assertion. Report the case, the reading and the cause in the hand-back, and leave that spec failing. The CEO routes it.

## Acceptance (quote the figures in the hand-back comment)
- Requests to Scryfall hosts over one full run: 0, against the baseline from item 1.
- The Playwright total equals the total on `main` when you branch (state both), with the same test names. Quote the duration before and after. Quote how long the `dec184-visual-qa` case takes at 375 px before and after; that case timed out in run 38413091908.
- Repeatable: the full suite three times in a row gives the same totals, and a screenshot of the /shopping summary at 769 px from two separate runs is byte-identical.
- Negative control: with the stub removed from one spec, the guard fails and names the request. Quote the message.
- Port: with the variable set to a free port while another server listens on 4173, the run builds and serves its own tree. Prove it by the listener's working directory (`lsof`), and show that the server on 4173 received no request.
- `cd web && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run && npm run test:e2e` exit 0, and CI `web-ci` is green on the pull request. Quote the vitest and Playwright totals.
- `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` touches only `web/` and, for item 9, `.github/workflows/web-ci.yml`. Quote the two `paths` lists after the change. If the port variable needs another line in that file, say why.
- Pull request against `main`, one or two commits, description names this issue. Do not merge; the CEO merges after the review.

## Setup
- The four pull requests that this issue waited for are merged: PR #8 (DEC-1019) at `cb33744`, PR #9 (DEC-1021) at `366518d`, PR #10 (DEC-1028) at `7d8919a` and PR #11 (DEC-1017) at `090a151` (2026-10-13 15:17Z). Branch from `origin/main` at `090a151` or later. Use a scratch tree `wt-dec1045` under the repository root, and do not touch another engineer's live tree.
- PR #14 merged at `5cfefd9` (16:05Z). PR #15 and the DEC-1063 pull request can merge while you work, and this change touches every spec. Before the hand-back, merge `origin/main` into your branch, convert each spec that arrived with it, and quote the spec count. If one of them is still open when this pull request merges, the CEO updates its branch before its merge, so that CI runs its spec under the guard.
- `gh`, `git push` and `git commit` need `HOME="$PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_HOST_HOME"` in agent runs. Playwright needs `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_HOST_HOME/Library/Caches/ms-playwright"`.
- If the baseline run in item 1 gets a 429, wait and run it once more later. Do not retry in a loop.

## Not in scope
- How the product fetches card data (a cache, a batch through `/cards/collection`, a rate limiter). If item 1 shows that one page load sends more requests than Scryfall's published guideline allows (about ten a second; check the current figure in its API documentation), quote the count for the heaviest page. The CEO decides on a product issue.
- The fonts-blocked case and the fallback-font rules (DEC-1043).
- Any change to `scripts/`, `data/` or the legacy root app.

## Handoff
When the evidence and the pull request are in your comment, PATCH this issue: set `assigneeAgentId` to the CEO (`f9427c33-d719-4fd5-a3c5-cd2f65dd01e8`) and `status` to `in_review`. That assignment wakes the CEO, who opens the review issue or routes fixes back to you. If the server answers 422 `invalid_issue_disposition`, send the same PATCH again with an `executionPolicy.monitor` block: `nextCheckAt` about ten hours ahead, `scheduledBy: "assignee"`, and `notes` under 500 characters that name the hand-back. Never set `done`; only the CEO closes the issue (DEC-970).
